architecture_decision:
Insert an unnumbered `## Glossary` section in `docs/command-journal-contract.md` immediately after the end of `## 12. Founder ruling — terminal semantics for non-dispatch authority acts — [RULED]` (line 728) and immediately before `## Changelog` (line 729). Placing `## Glossary` as an unnumbered reference section after `§12` and before `## Changelog` preserves the exact section numbers `§1` through `§12` cited throughout the contract, test files, and `packages/journal/` specifications, while keeping `## Changelog` at the tail of the document as its chronological revision log.

Begin `## Glossary` with a single boundary sentence: `This glossary summarizes terms defined in §§1–12 for reader navigation; it creates no independent rule, and on any conflict the operative clauses in §§1–12 govern.`

Structure `## Glossary` as a Markdown table (`| Term | Definition | Governing section(s) |`) organized in alphabetical order of `Term`, covering the contract's closed terminology across six categories:
1. Record classes and chain model: `chain_hash`, `command` (record class), `decision` (record class), `genesis constant`, `record_class`, `seq`.
2. Command projection elements and identities (`§2` elements 1–11): `actor_id` / `role_id`, `authorization_ref`, `command_envelope`, `command_id`, `dispatch_state`, `envelope_digest`, `evidence_refs`, `init_model` / `provider_conversation_id`, `intended_provider` / `intended_model` / `intended_surface`, `lifecycle_event_ref`, `outcome`, `provider` / `model` / `execution_surface`, `recorded_at`, `repository` / `scope_ref`, `room_id` / `run_id` / `execution_id` (set-once identities).
3. Command event vocabulary and reconciliation (`§5`): `completed`, `dispatched`, `failed`, `identity_bound`, `journaled`, `reconciled` / `ambiguous` / `mismatch` (`resolution_semantics`), `resolved`, `unresolved`.
4. Decision record state and plan-hash derivation (`§2`, `§7`, `§8`, `§12`): `effective plan-bearing state`, `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN`, `plan_hash`, `prior_state`, `recorded_state` (recorded lifecycle state at the decision).
5. Storage locus and sole-writer enforcement (`§1.4`, `§3`, `§4.1`): `build_room_events`, `command_journal_chain_head`, `command_journal_events`, `command_journal_writer`, `head_id`.
6. Canonical serialization specifications (`§6.2`): `BRJ:a:1`, `BRJ:b:1`, `BRJ:c:1`, `BRJ:c:2`, `BRJ:d:1`.

interfaces_and_contracts:
No TypeScript interfaces, SQL schemas, HTTP endpoints, or binary serialization formats (`BRJ:a:1`, `BRJ:b:1`, `BRJ:c:1`, `BRJ:c:2`, `BRJ:d:1`) are changed. Within `docs/command-journal-contract.md`, the `## Glossary` section must conform to the exact terminology and definitions established in `§§1–12`:
- `actor_id` / `role_id`: Registry-valid actor and role identifiers for a command (`§2` element 3, line 140); for `decision` records, actor is always `founder` (`§2`, line 159).
- `authorization_ref`: Reference to the governing authorization or approval (`§2` element 7, line 144; `§2`, line 162). For a command to reach `completed` (directly or via `resolved`), `authorization_ref` must resolve to an existing, valid, applicable authorization whose granted scope covers the observed `(provider, model, execution_surface)` (`§5.3`, lines 387–413).
- `BRJ:a:1`: Version 1 canonical byte serialization specification (`packages/journal/specs/serialization-a-envelope.md`) for the normalized command envelope (`§6.2(a)`, lines 472, 499–500).
- `BRJ:b:1`: Version 1 canonical byte serialization specification (`packages/journal/specs/serialization-b-plandoc.md`) for the PlanDoc digest (`§6.2(b)`, lines 472, 501–502).
- `BRJ:c:1`: Version 1 canonical byte serialization specification (`packages/journal/specs/serialization-c-command-row.md`) for the complete `command`-class event row (`§6.2(c)`, lines 472–477, 510–517).
- `BRJ:c:2`: Version 2 canonical byte serialization specification (`packages/journal/specs/serialization-c-command-row-v2.md`) for the complete `command`-class event row, adding `init_model` and `provider_conversation_id` on `dispatched`; a chain's command rows move from `BRJ:c:1` to `BRJ:c:2` once and never back (`§2` element 4, line 141; `§6.2(c)`, lines 510–517).
- `BRJ:d:1`: Version 1 canonical byte serialization specification (`packages/journal/specs/serialization-d-decision-row.md`) for the complete `decision`-class record row (`§6.2(d)`, lines 477–489).
- `build_room_events`: The ratified `DEC-20260815-11` lifecycle state machine event log table, authoritative for room lifecycle transitions (`§1.4`, lines 63–110).
- `chain_hash`: 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest over the prior row's 64 lowercase-hex ASCII `chain_hash` bytes (or the 64-ASCII-zero genesis constant for `seq = 1`) concatenated with the row's canonical byte sequence per specification (c) or (d) (`§4.1`, lines 273–290; `§6.2`, lines 495–507).
- `command` (record class): The journal record class for governed commands, consisting of append-only events (`journaled`, `identity_bound`, `dispatched`, `completed`, `failed`, `unresolved`, `resolved`) projected by `command_id` across the global `seq` chain (`§1.2`, lines 50–53; `§2`, lines 114–149; `§5.2`, lines 359–377).
- `command_envelope`: The post-redaction normalized representation of an authorized command (`§2` element 6, line 143; `§6.1`, lines 463–467).
- `command_id`: Unique command identifier in the dedicated `cmd_` namespace, serving as the projection grouping key (`§2` element 1, lines 115–116, 138) and end-to-end dispatch idempotency key (`§5.3`, lines 428–432).
- `command_journal_chain_head`: Dedicated singleton Postgres table (`head_id = 1` check constraint) holding the mutable serialization latch (current tail `seq` and `chain_hash`) initialized to `seq = 0` and the 64-zero genesis constant by migration, verified against the event tail inside every append transaction, and carrying no journal authority (`§3`, lines 227–231; `§4.1`, lines 291–328).
- `command_journal_events`: Dedicated append-only Postgres table storing one row per journal record (`command` event or `decision` record) ordered by global `seq` (`§3`, lines 227–235; `§4.1`, lines 283–287).
- `command_journal_writer`: Dedicated Postgres database role that is the sole role granted `INSERT` on `command_journal_events` and `UPDATE` on `command_journal_chain_head` (`§3`, lines 236–247; `§4.1`, lines 319–328).
- `completed`: Terminal command event representing verified successful execution; requires a prior `dispatched` event, an observed identity matching the journaled intended routing identity, and a resolvable `authorization_ref` whose granted scope covers the observed `(provider, model, execution_surface)` (`§5.2`, line 373; `§5.3`, lines 387–413).
- `decision` (record class): Distinct journal record class on the shared `seq` chain for Founder decision acts (T4 `plan.revision_requested`, T5 `plan.approved`, T22 `founder.cancel`). Each `decision` record is a single event, terminal by construction, with no state machine, no `command_id`, and `§2` elements 1, 4, 8, and 9 not applicable (`§1.2`, lines 50–53; `§2`, lines 153–218; `§12`, lines 654–728).
- `dispatch_state`: Derived projection field (`§2` element 8, line 145) equal to the `event_type` of the latest event for a `command_id`; never stored as a mutable column (`§5.4`, lines 444–450).
- `dispatched`: Command event recorded at most once after `journaled` (and after `identity_bound` if present), carrying the authoritative observed routing identity (`provider`, `model`, `execution_surface`, and under `BRJ:c:2` optional `init_model` and `provider_conversation_id`) (`§2` element 4, lines 126–134, 141; `§5.2`, lines 371–372).
- `effective plan-bearing state`: For a `decision` record, the recorded lifecycle state at the decision with `RECONCILING` resolved to its stored `prior_state`; governs whether `plan_hash` is absent (`ROOM_CREATED`, `SCOPED`, `PLANNING`) or required (`§2`, lines 165–197).
- `envelope_digest`: 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest over the canonical byte sequence of `command_envelope` per specification (a) (`§2` element 6, line 143; `§6.2`, lines 495–500).
- `evidence_refs`: Ordered array of pointers into the evidence store carried on a journal row without inlining payloads (`§2` element 10, line 147; `§6.2(c)`, lines 474–475).
- `failed`: Terminal command event following `dispatched`, or following `journaled` / `identity_bound` directly only when the attempt provably never left the gateway boundary; carries a `failure_classification` (`§5.2`, line 373; `§5.3`, lines 414–418).
- `genesis constant`: The prior-hash input for the first row (`seq = 1`) and the migration-initialized hash on `command_journal_chain_head` (`seq = 0`), consisting of 64 ASCII `0` characters (`§4.1`, lines 288–290, 304–309; `§6.2`, lines 503–507).
- `head_id`: Primary key of `command_journal_chain_head`, pinned by `CHECK (head_id = 1)` so only a single row can exist (`§4.1`, lines 319–328).
- `identity_bound`: Optional one-time command event occurring only between `journaled` and `dispatched` to bind element-2 identities (`room_id`, `run_id`, `execution_id`) that did not yet exist at `journaled` (`§2`, lines 121–126; `§5.2`, lines 367–371).
- `init_model` / `provider_conversation_id`: Optional fields on `dispatched` (introduced in `v0.18` under `BRJ:c:2`) recording the model named by the executor's init event before work was sent and the provider conversation identifier from that event (`§2` element 4, line 141; `§6.2`, lines 510–517).
- `intended_provider` / `intended_model` / `intended_surface`: Pre-dispatch intended routing identity recorded on `journaled` and labeled as intent (`§2` element 4, lines 126–128, 141; `§5.2`, lines 364–366).
- `journaled`: Mandatory first event for every `command_id`, durably committed before dispatch (`§5.1`, lines 352–354; `§5.2`, lines 364–366; `§5.3`, lines 378–380).
- `lifecycle_event_ref`: The normative pair `(`room_id`, `event_id`)` referencing the corresponding row in `build_room_events` (`§1.4`, lines 81–88; `§2`, lines 162–163).
- `outcome`: Derived projection field (`§2` element 9, line 146) representing the command's terminal determination (`completed` or `failed`, directly or via `resolved`), `unresolved` while an `unresolved` event is unreconciled, and pending otherwise (`§5.4`, lines 444–450).
- `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN`: Ruled control-plane credential configured in `packages/control-plane/src/config.ts` (at least 32 characters, distinct from `CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN`) required to authenticate Founder plan decisions at the control plane in Phase 4 (`§8.2`, lines 562–571).
- `plan_hash`: 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest over the canonical byte sequence of a PlanDoc per specification (b); computed at T3 (`plan.submitted`), matched at T5 (`plan.approved`), and carried on `decision` records whenever the effective plan-bearing state is not in `{ROOM_CREATED, SCOPED, PLANNING}` (`§2`, lines 161–206; `§6.2`, lines 501–502; `§7.1`, lines 528–530).
- `prior_state`: The non-terminal, non-`RECONCILING` lifecycle state stored on entry to `RECONCILING` (T19), carried alongside `recorded_state` on a `decision` record when the decision fires from `RECONCILING` (`§2`, lines 160–183, 199–203).
- `provider` / `model` / `execution_surface`: Authoritative observed actual routing identity recorded on `dispatched` (`§2` element 4, lines 127–134, 141; `§5.2`, lines 371–372).
- `reconciled` / `ambiguous` / `mismatch`: The consumed 3.5 reconciliation semantics carried on `resolved` (and `mismatch` for cross-store disagreement under `§1.4`), where `ambiguous` never resolves silently (`§1.4`, lines 100–102; `§5.2`, lines 374–377).
- `record_class`: Explicit discriminator field (`command` or `decision`) carried on every journal row and included in the canonical byte input to `chain_hash` (`§1.2`, lines 50–53; `§2`, lines 215–218; `§6.2`, lines 487–489).
- `recorded_at`: Server-generated timestamp on every journal row (`§2` element 11, line 148).
- `recorded_state`: The lifecycle state from which a Founder decision act fired, recorded positively on every `decision` record (`§2`, lines 159–161, 199–203).
- `repository` / `scope_ref`: Immutable repository and governed scope input recorded on `journaled` (`§2` element 5, line 142).
- `resolved`: Terminal command event permitted only after `unresolved` (at most once), carrying the reconciled terminal determination (`completed` or `failed`), reconciliation semantics (`reconciled`, `ambiguous`, or `mismatch`), and reconciliation evidence (`§5.2`, lines 373–377; `§5.3`, lines 382–383, 408–413).
- `room_id` / `run_id` / `execution_id`: Element-2 identities that are set-once (null only before the identity exists, recorded on `journaled`, `identity_bound`, or `dispatched`, and immutable thereafter) (`§2` element 2, lines 121–126, 139).
- `seq`: Server-generated global monotonic sequence number across the single canonical journal chain (`§1.2`, lines 50–53; `§2` element 11, line 148; `§4.1`, lines 283–287, 329).
- `unresolved`: Command event appended when provider contact cannot be ruled out (or when authorization coverage is indeterminate); blocks any completion claim or retry until `resolved` (`§5.2`, line 373; `§5.3`, lines 399–402, 419–425; `§5.5`, lines 451–455).
